Voron (anvoron1@yandex.ru) October 13, 2026 Abstract Based on calculated and recorded data, this paper demonstrates the use of two length systems – the metric system and the ancient Egyptian system (royal cubit) – by the builders of the Giza plateau. The study analyzes the numerical linear dimensions of each pyramid in the Giza pyramid complex, as well as the base area and visible surface area of the complex pyramids. Spatial 3D segments were obtained, which formed the basis for calculating the areas of two triangles formed by the peaks of the Menkaure, Khafre, and Khufu pyramids and the highest point of the "Great Sphinx" monument. 1 Introduction Prior studies conducted by the author [1, 2, 3] indicated that mathematical regularities, specifically the Fibonacci numbers, are encoded within the parameters of the Giza plateau pyramids. The present study aims to harmonize individual data into a unified, logically coherent system, allowing for the formulation of a scientific hypothesis. The objective of this work is to calculate the spatial (3D) parameters of the triangles formed by the physical peaks of the three Giza plateau pyramids and the highest point of the "Great Sphinx" monument to search for numerical patterns. 2 The main part Research Methodology. This paper utilizes a method of comparative analysis matching recorded geometric parameters of the objects against their theoretical calculated models, adjusted for the thickness of the lost casing stones and structural degradation. Using artificial intelligence tools, true spatial 3D segments between key objects were reconstructed based on our previous research. The calculation of the areas of the formed triangles was performed using the ancient Egyptian unit of length, the "Royal Cubit" (0.5236 m). content_preview: The Number 137 in Physics: Fine-Structure Constant, Quantum Effects, and the Nuclear Stability Limit in LEDM V. F. Strohm Independent Researcher E-mail: vfnv@mail.ru, vfstrohm@yahoo.de DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23342672 Abstract In fundamental physics, the fine-structure constant is traditionally introduced as an empirical dimensionless parameter that determines the strength of the electromagnetic interaction. In this paper, within the framework of the Local Energy Deficit Model (LEDM), an analytical derivation of the constant is presented from the first principles of the mechanics of an isotropic elastic vacuum substrate. It is shown that the inverse quantity represents a fundamental geometric-dynamical invariant of a threedimensional medium defined by spatial normalization ( ), the number of shear degrees of freedom of the stress deviator ( ), the spectral integral of zero-point fluctuations, and SU(2) spinor topology. A systematic analysis of physical phenomena associated with the number 137 is carried out, including the electron velocity on the first Bohr orbit, the fine structure of spectra, the convergence of quantum electrodynamics (QED) series, the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron (g - 2), and the critical Schwinger limit. On this basis, the physical and mechanical nature of the "running coupling constant" is revealed as a nonlinear elastic response of the medium (Hooke's law) under strong deformations, and a mechanicaltopological solution to the "Feynman paradox" for element 137 of the periodic table is proposed. Keywords: fine-structure constant; number 137; Local Energy Deficit Model (LEDM); elastic vacuum substrate; shear degrees of freedom; atomic spectra; quantum electrodynamics; anomalous magnetic moment; Schwinger limit; superheavy nuclei; SU(2). 1. The study aimed to derive another equation in which the average ionization energies of hydrogen and any other multielectron atom are independent variables. The objective was to answer the question in the literature that states, "Are Slater’s Rules the Best Approach for Calculating Effective Nuclear Charge for Undergraduates?" (Moore & Birnbaum, 2014) and compare the graphical portrayal of chemical periodicity between outcomes using data generated using Slater's rules for some elements and data generated in this research. By exploring theoretical and computational methods and the data in the literature, the study showed that ENC (1.34458-3.32446) for the first 30 elements computed using the 2021 CODATA fine structure constant (FSC, for short) was higher than those (1.344023.32309) without it; however, the equation containing the computed FSC using e^2/20 hc and other equations gave the same value of ENC. The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus atomic number (Z) did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). title: Survive the Field: Why the BBP Machine Has Its Form
content_preview: Qu Harmonics – The incomplete Universe Copyright Dean A. Kulik – Orcid ID # 0009-0003-3128-8828 Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC 4.0) github.com/QuHarmonics/The-Nexus-Harmonic-Reality info@quharmonics.com Page | 1 Survive the Field: Why the BBP Machine Has Its Form Rational wheels, rigid lanes, layers as atoms, nesting depth, and the same Mold in a compiler Driven by Dean A. Kulik October, 2025 Abstract This sequel to Nest, Run, Fold [1] asks why the BBP digit machine has the Form found there, and whether that Form belongs to π or to any machine that transforms without forgetting. The guiding picture is a runner crossing a field: nothing is accumulated, the starting point fixes how much field lies ahead, and a process is complex to the extent that it survives the whole field. Five answers come from the machine itself. The fold wheels s = 1/(1 − z), |z| = 1, that close on a rational number are exactly the crystallographic rotations; only the quarter and third turns both turn and shrink, and base 16 is (1 − i)8 . By Baker’s theorem the eight base-16 lanes satisfy exactly one rational relation, so the Adamchik–Wagon line holds every π formula on them, while the twelve base-729 lanes of the 30° wheel satisfy two. The four lanes of a layer are copies of one motion that agree on about 2 log16 k digits, and a layer is heard only through their difference. Each vanishing moment of the weights adds log k digits of silence, and as many can vanish as there are relations: one for BBP, two for the ternary machine, which has a unique doubly crested formula for π√3. An involution in a loop silences exactly the harmonics it reflects. The same Mold then appears in a compiler. Each SHA-256 round and its message schedule are Molds, so for every message the 64 rounds permute the state and keep its past with no stack.
